text:
William Nylander's name is everywhere this week, and not for his hands. Toronto is in a long winless run, the head coach has publicly called out his costly mistakes, and the trade speculation has followed (Elliotte Friedman has reported the Leafs would need to be mindful of his trade list if they go down that road). That's the backdrop for a player with 11 goals and 25 points in 26 games.

The season line is fine. The last ten games are not: four points where we'd expect about ten at his ice time. That slump is some of each. He's on the ice for a few fewer chances than usual, and the ones he does get aren't going in. Over the full season he's shooting 18% on 8.5 expected goals, close to his usual, so the goals were never the problem.

The worry is the other end. Toronto gets just 43% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, and Evolving-Hockey had the same weakness last season: opponents generated noticeably more with him out there, against top competition. Watch whether the chances against settle. That, more than the trade chatter, decides how this season reads.
headline: Nylander's slump, and the chances against
